title: Data and analysis scripts: Comparing XR and Desktop Interfaces for Shape-Form Estimation and Manipulation in a Scientific Context
description:
Supporting material for the manuscript Comparing XR and Desktop Interfaces for Shape-Form Estimation and Manipulation in a Scientific Context, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics.

Three between-subjects experiments (N = 64; domain experts and novices) comparing an immersive XR interface against a conventional desktop interface for interactive superquadric shape estimation, in a task context drawn from a soft-robotic jamming-gripper design workflow.

Contents: a de-identified per-participant dataset (64 × 112); an analysis script reproducing the reported expertise-by-interface interaction tests via aligned rank transform; an independent reimplementation of the Barr normalised implicit distance with its validation against meshes of known parameters; and the study stimuli and derived result workbooks.

De-identification: participants are identified only by a pseudonymous ID, age is released in bands rather than exact years, and free-text response columns have been removed. The raw participant workbook is not included.

Licensing is split: the analysis code is released under the MIT licence, and the data, meshes and textures under CC BY 4.0.
